task.prompt: Inspect the slash commands actually registered on the currently bound synthetic app synthetic-evaluation-app. In this fixture, enabled means currently registered; there is no separate enable/disable state. List the registered commands and identify the enabled command. Do not create, update, delete, install, or change anything. Return JSON with commands (an array of objects containing command_id and command) and enabled_command (the command name without its leading slash).

limitations: The predeclared name=status, enabled=true fixture is mapped to command=status in the API list. The frozen implementation does not expose a distinct enabled field or enable/disable operation; the prompt explicitly defines enabled as registered for this development task.
This verifies read-only registration inspection, not lifecycle writes, enablement configuration, app installation, backend scopes, private live app visibility or five-minute client caching.
The v7 slash-command endpoint is absent from the frozen generated catalog. Both the existing shortcut and generic raw GET are valid; do not invent a generated application command.
The synthetic fixture contains no live account, app or tenant credentials. Official and next use the same isolated authsidecar binding and backend.
Help/schema discovery and output projection/detail choices are permitted. Correctness is based on actual reads, answer and state invariants; token/API costs are separate measurements.
No model runs were performed for this contract. The evaluator must implement and test route handling and independent verification before marking the adapter executable.

The GET list endpoint has no supported query or body selector: it returns commands for the bound app. The static table is sufficient for this one-item, unpaginated read; it does not emulate arbitrary unverified query parameters or mutations. Both signed user and bot identities use the same public response.

The sidecar ledger must independently observe application_slash_command_list and no rejected or mutable requests. Immutable fixture command content plus the common config-state comparison establish this bounded no-change task; no agent-authored receipt is trusted.

Actual route/response evidence: shortcuts/application/slash_command_list.go, shortcuts/application/slash_command_list_test.go, tests/cli_e2e/application/slash_command_dryrun_test.go, and tests/next_sections/application/application_e2e_test.go. This normalization has not been run through evaluator-controlled binary tests.
